summary: A CCC stone tower on Mount Constitution in Moran State Park, built 1935-36, once a fire lookout; now a state park attraction open to visitors.

facts.design: Five-story sandstone tower with a live-in top-floor observatory, designed by Seattle architect Ellsworth Storey

staffing.status: no longer staffed for fire detection

access.note: A popular state park attraction; the register says the state parks commission maintains the stone tower. Island Histories says visitors can drive to the top or hike or bike up.

visit.drive_up: Drive to the top, or park at the bottom and hike or bike up about seven miles (Island Histories)

facts.agency: Washington State Parks and Recreation Commission

events.note: CCC crew of 28 began constructing the stone tower in August 1935
Topping out celebrated July 7, 1936; tower completed later that year. Island Histories gives 1935-36. The register gives 1937.
Little Summit Lookout, 1.5 miles south, built as a replacement after tourists interfered with firewatching
Division of Forestry staffing ended in 1967; a second, more isolated tower used solely for detection followed. Firelookout.com says mid-1960s.
A plan to demolish the tower was thwarted by Orcas Island residents; KVOS agreed to restore it and moved its equipment to a new steel tower beside it
Placed on the National Register of Historic Places
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, June 19, 1993
Restoration in 2003 and 2004 under local contractor Rolf Eriksen; rededication attended by CCC veterans in May 2004

corrections.why: No source read gives 1930. HistoryLink dates the start of construction to August 1935 and completion to later in 1936; Island Histories gives 1935-36. The register gives 1937 and firelookout.com says mid-1930s.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: HistoryLink and Island Histories agree on 1935-36, with a detailed construction account in HistoryLink. The register's 1937 and firelookout.com's mid-1930s are reported as variants.
Island Histories gives 53 feet, which matches the record's 16.1 m. Firelookout.com gives 45 feet. Both are reported; the record's 16.1 m is kept.
The register says Division of Forestry staffing ended in 1967. Firelookout.com says the lookout served until the mid-1960s and that the replacement was built in 1966. Both are reported.
HistoryLink credits Ellsworth Storey with the design. Island Histories credits Roland Koepf working under Storey's direction. Both are reported.

The register gives 2,332 ft (711 m), which matches the record's elevation_m of 710.8. Firelookout.com gives 2407 ft, and HistoryLink gives 2,409 ft for the summit. The register's figure is for the tower site.

notes_for_editor: Build year: the record's 1930 appears in none of the sources read. HistoryLink and Island Histories put construction in 1935-36 and the register says 1937, so the correction is to 1935-36. Height: the record's 16.1 m matches Island Histories' 53 feet; firelookout.com's 45 feet disagrees. Staffing end: 1966 (firelookout) versus 1967 (register). Designer: Storey (HistoryLink) versus Koepf under Storey (Island Histories). Access is public, per Island Histories and HistoryLink. The stone tower's interior visitor access was not confirmed, so the story does not say visitors can climb it. Read budget: five page reads (NHLR, firelookout.com, HistoryLink twice, Island Histories), within the cap of six. The search snippet for the Island Histories page was checked by fetch before use. The 1930 build date in the record probably comes from a source not read here; it is not repeated in any source this run found.
